qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Three-pointed star brand equity, premier engineering heritage, and commercial van dominance (Sprinter) provide brand premium over volume OEMs. However, pricing power has proven cyclical rather than structural, as top-end luxury EV push (EQS/EQE) met customer resistance and Chinese luxury buyers rotated to domestic tech-forward EV offerings. Group ROCE declined to 6.8% in 2024 (multi-cycle average 8-10%, failing the 12% hurdle). Key threats: China volume/pricing collapse, EV transition friction, and unionized manufacturing cost structures.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% & pricing power, REJECT). Mercedes-Benz's 'top-end luxury' strategy failed to establish durable pricing power beyond the post-pandemic supply constraint windfall. Group ROCE declined to 6.8% in 2024 (multi-cycle ROCE 8-10% vs 12% hurdle), with cars division RoS compressing to 8-10%. High German manufacturing cost structure, heavy EV capex, and severe market share losses to Chinese luxury EVs in Asia erode economic returns.
qualitative.evidence: Group ROCE contracted from 10.1% in 2022 to 10.0% in 2023 and 6.8% in 2024. Adjusted Return on Sales (RoS) for Mercedes-Benz Cars dropped from 14.6% in 2022 to ~8-10% in 2024. Multi-cycle ROIC averages below 9%, failing the 12% hurdle. In China, which accounted for over a third of high-margin S-Class and Maybach sales, local EV competition and macroeconomic softening triggered deep discounting. Heavy dual capex/R&D spending across internal combustion, hybrid, and battery-electric architectures restricts incremental capital returns.
